title: PRESSER | Yolett McPhee-McCuin - Alabama A&M Postgame (11-22-26)
text: Let's give your opening statement on the win against Alabama&M 66 to 47. >> Uh first of all, just want to give credit to Alabama&M. I really like the tenacity and um they played with I thought they came in fairless and I expect them to do well in the swack uh this year. Um the head coach is a good friend of mine and so uh we spent a lot of time talking about what we want things to look like and and I definitely saw what they were trying to do and I thought um and they tested us a lot today. Uh as far as our uh the the game is concerned. I was grateful for the crowd. I thought we had a great crowd. Uh I know the holidays are coming up so some people are here, some people aren't. But I really appreciate everybody coming out uh to support this team as we are a work in progress. Uh as far as the game is concerned um you know we we are going to be just a team that's going to continuously figure it out. I think uh one of the things that is difficult for all humans is to try to compare. But comparison is the thief of of joy. This team will have its own uh journey. And so this is the journey that they're on. There were a lot of things that we did that I really liked. I thought Jada Rishard is trying to do what I'm asking her to do. So I saw a lot of victory in that. Um and I'm definitely going to celebrate that with her. Um as far uh where we go next, we we we still not rebounding well. That's something that is uh something that we have to uh look to improve on. Uh but uh ever since we got back from Ohio State, you know, I've been really really tough on this team and um I thought the ones that did get in and fight, I thought they fought pretty hard, so I was happy about that. >> Coach, just at the very beginning of the game, right before it starts, Eric, she was obviously on your staff just a couple years ago. To have that moment with her and to see how her group has progressed, how cool is that? >> I mean, it was amazing. And I mean Erica is is Oxford, you know, she loves this place. I remember when she came in to help me out. I think it was at a as a GA and then she was so good. I asked the administration to create a position so that we could keep her on staff. Um, and then I knew she was ready to spread her wings and so she got an opportunity at Alabama&M with a good friend of mine. Uh, but she she love loves Oxford. Uh the head coach says she's always here on her free time. Uh and you didn't see what was in the bag, but it was a chicken in the stick on the stick. So that was her favorite delicacy uh when she was here, that chicken on the stick. She had the whole staff eating a chicken on the stick. Uh but this game was special for me because one of my former players, coaches on the staff as well from Jacksonville. So, uh, anytime we play them, I just really enjoy just just getting out there and competing with them. >> I guess moments in this game. How do you, as a coach, maintain your team's aggression without going over the edge? >> Yeah, I mean, here's the thing. I have a personal relationship with the Alabama&M program. Like, I support them in a bunch of different ways. I know them. They know me. So, I knew they would want to come out and play well. and and that's why you have to respect everybody and respect the game. I didn't think anything was um excessive. I thought they just came out and played hard and the first time they played a P4 team, they didn't look really well. So, they wanted to come out and and be competitive and um you know, and and fix what they didn't do right the first time. They had just got off a big win. We had just got off of a loss that was a incredibly emotional toll on us and physically when I was done with them the last 48 hours. So, you know, um I knew it would be this type of game and and I saw a lot of resilience in certain people. I was happy for that. >> What can you say about the second half and how they responded to your message? >> Um you know, we we got to figure out how to be a two a two half team. Uh we're going to take more bumps before we figure it out. Uh the lessons is seems like in this team seems to be in the loss, but um you know hopefully we can show them some film. We're not able to go on our a trip. We had uh our tournament got the game got cancelled. So we're here this week and I had been pouting about it for about a month a month. But now I'm like really happy about it cuz we need the week. Um we need to make some things clear. We need to um be bought into what we're trying to do and figure out what what that needs to look like, especially before we play Memphis. >> Speaking of Memphis, um anything you've seen on film early on? I know you had prepared for this game today. Anything you've seen from them? >> Yeah, I've watched a lot of their games cuz I I really like the coach. I have a lot of respect for her. I just think they play incredibly hard. They're going to come in with no fear. Uh no matter what we believe as a team, anytime you have a team that is not a part of the P5 that has a chance to come and play a P4, P5 team, they're going to they're going to uh bring their best effort. So, we can expect that. But this will be a great week. I'll make sure, you know, there's some things as a coach, you know, I have to assess, too. you know, I'm not going to put it all on our team as we're growing. Uh, as they're growing, I think we're all growing. I'm figuring out what works for them. They're figuring out what the miss way looks like. And if we just continue to stick together, I think um my goal is for every game for us to look better. You know, when we played Ohio State, that was a disappointing loss for all of us. We did not feel like we should have lost that game, but we also didn't think that we did what we needed to do in order to win the game. You know, most times when games end up to last shot, anybody can win or lose those games, but there were some things we could control that I didn't think we did that. Uh, so we're going to use this week to just get better and uh get some rest and then prepare ourselves for for Memphis, which I expect to be a good game. >> Coach, you briefly mentioned Jada Rashard and you know, some of the victories that you're taking on tonight, right? She spoke on how you've been really tough on her. What were some of those conversations like with her and some of those personal victories that you saw on her today? Yeah, I mean I think uh you know the internet gets caught up in like numbers and and and all of the things that doesn't matter when it comes to players getting coming into a new role. You know, uh Jada Rishard at her old school was called the played the PG position, but she wasn't a point guard. You know, that their program kind of ran itself. Now she's in a situation where she has to be the leader on the team. this is new territory for her and she didn't doesn't really know what that looks like. So, it's my job to help her uh do that and I think in the long run it'll be incredibly beneficial for her because um that's what she's going to want to need to do if she wants to play at the next level and this is the ownership she's going to have to take if she wants to help us win the games that we need to win so that we can put ourselves in postseason um conversation. And with her having a career high tonight, obviously you said you don't get too caught up in confidence, but for her her to have a career performance tonight after being tough on her, what does that say about her? >> Well, tonight was was totally a game where she made the game easy and was in was coachable. I felt like she was the most coachable this game than any other game we've had, which is great because we've talked about certain reads, the type of shots she she should take, uh what we need from her, and um she's learning. One thing I don't question when it comes to Jada is like her intent and our in our motive and our heart and she's just she's just a fighter and a competitor. Her best days are ahead of her. So, uh, I'm just as a staff, we're just going to try to guide her as best as possible, but, uh, hopefully tonight she sees the reward in her buying into what we've been asking her to do. >> Denila also said that you've been tough on her, especially when it comes to to rebounding. Um, in in a perfect world when this thing really clicks for you all, what what do you see her role actually being on on this team? >> Uh, she had eight and eight. You know, I could live with that. uh when and as we go through I mean uh Nebe in my opinion is an X factor for this team. Um I'm not hard on people I don't believe in. If I don't believe in you, I'm I'm probably I don't I'm not hard on you. And uh so I'm hard and so right now they probably all feel like I believe in them because I'm hard on every last one of them. Uh but Nebe I there's [clears throat] something in her that I know that she can bring to the table. Um, and uh, we really need her to do that on a consistent basis. And so, uh, she I thought she played hard today. I thought she did a lot of the things we're asking her to do. And we're going to continue to challenge both her um, uh, Desiree. Uh, Desire's numbers don't look good as far as in the stats, but she's someone that we're going to rely on tremendously as as we go through the season. Thank you. Happy Thanksgiving to all that celebrate.
